--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Alex, I'll run the POC logistics, Samir here is our SE, Maya's CSM who'll help with onboarding. Jordan, do you want to kick off with the goals you guys have for the POC?
[00:32] Jordan (Gamma - CTO): Yeah thanks. Main thing is we want to validate latency and cost for our new customer support assistant. We already did some internal tests but we need a realistic end-to-end benchmark and to understand concurrency behavior, like how many simultaneous sessions we can support.
[01:05] Priya (Head of ML): Also important: output quality mustn't degrade with batching/quantization. Our success criteria are both latency and semantic parity with our current model. We'll define exact accuracy/regression checks but initial SLOs are 95th percentile latency under 500 milliseconds for interactive flows.
[01:38] Samir (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say interactive flows, is that single-turn chat or multi-turn with context? That changes KV cache behavior and token footprint.
[02:05] Jordan: Mostly multi-turn, up to 6 turns, average session length ~3 turns, we keep about 2k tokens context sometimes but typical is much smaller — maybe 1k. We use RAG on some queries, so there is a retrieval step pre-tokenization, often adds 100-800 tokens to inputs depending on doc length.
[02:42] Alex: Good — that's helpful. Priya, do you have empirical numbers on QPS right now? Baseline / peak?
[03:05] Priya: Baseline average is around 50 QPS across our customer base. We see spikes during morning batch times up to 180-220 QPS for short windows, maybe 3-5 minutes. Concurrent sessions are usually around 120 active sessions during peak.
[03:33] Ben (Infra): And to add, our infra currently allows about 1Gbps egress per region, and we have a VPC with strict outbound rules; any suggestion on networking for dedicated deployment?
[03:58] Samir: For Dedicated we typically provide VPC peering or private link. We'll need your network CIDRs and firewall rules; we can do an initial throughput estimate assuming 50 QPS and average token sizes. We'll also want to test with your real sample logs.
[04:25] Lina (Product): For success criteria besides latency we want cost estimates — like cost per 1k queries and cost per active session. We'd like Redwood to model cost with and without KV caching and different batching configs.
[04:48] Alex: Absolutely. Our Optimize team will provide configurations and cost modeling. For the POC we'll recommend a few profiles: latency-optimized (no aggressive batching), cost-balanced (small batching + KV caching), and max-cost-savings (larger batching, quantized models). We'll measure throughput, p95/p99 latency, and token-level cost.
[05:20] Priya: On token distribution — our sample shows input tokens median 65, mean 82, tail up to 800 when docs attached. Output tokens median 95, mean 120. Does that align with what Redwood needs to size instances?
[05:48] Samir: That's great and exactly the kind of distribution we need. For sizing, we care about average inference tokens per request (input+output) and the sequence length used for batch/kernels. If median is ~160 total tokens that's one thing, but the 800-token tails will impact memory and throughput.
[06:15] Jordan: Can you talk through how KV cache and multi-turn affect throughput and latency in Dedicated? We saw some notes about prefix caching but not sure of the tradeoffs.
[06:40] Samir: Sure. With multi-turn, caching KV states reduces recomputation for previous tokens; it helps latency for repeated context. However it increases memory footprint per session. Our runtime can pin KV to GPU memory and stream it; tradeoff is concurrent sessions vs memory. For your session counts (~120) and 1k token contexts occasionally, we'll need to model memory per session. We'll run a memory model in the sizing doc.
[07:12] Ben: Any rough starting recommendation? GPUs, instance counts?
[07:26] Samir: Based on initial numbers — 50 QPS baseline, median 160 tokens total — a couple of A40-class instances could handle baseline with batching and caching, but for the burst to ~200 QPS we'd look at autoscaling policies or a Dedicated pool of 4-6 GPUs to hit the target with p95 <500ms. We'll provide a few configurations in the sizing doc with expected cost estimates.
[07:58] Priya: For our internal regressions we run a 1k-prompt eval set. Would Redwood run the same eval during benchmark to check quality drift? How do you compare outputs to our golden set?
[08:20] Alex: Yes, we'll run your eval set. We usually do a token-level and semantic similarity check (ROUGE, embedding cosine) and flag regressions above your thresholds. We'll capture a diff and produce a report after the benchmark. If quantization causes degradation we'll show the tradeoff matrix.
[08:50] Jordan: Good. Timeline-wise, how long to stand up a POC if we sign for Dedicated trial? We're aiming for a 4-week POC.
[09:07] Maya (CSM): Operationally we can do onboarding in week 1 (networking, credentials), week 2 run baseline tests, week 3 run the full benchmark with your eval set, week 4 review results and tune. If you can get sample logs by end of this week we can shift earlier.
[09:38] Priya: We can export anonymized logs by Tuesday. They include time, prompt, response, session id, latency from our side. Is that format OK?
[09:55] Alex: Perfect, we'll provide a template. Include a sample of the heavy-tail requests.
[10:10] Ben: About the benchmark harness — do you require synthetic QPS generator or we'll replay logs?
[10:26] Samir: Both are fine; replay gives realism with session behavior but synthetic lets us ramp to exact QPS targets. For this POC we recommend a hybrid approach: replay for distribution and a synthetic ramp for peak stress tests. We'll share a k6-based harness and a Kubernetes job for replay.
[10:55] Priya: Any peculiarities around embeddings or rerank flows? We have a few endpoints that are embed-first then rerank which are more batchy but latency-sensitive.
[11:16] Samir: Embeddings are different — they are usually lower-latency but higher-throughput. For those flows we measure p95 separately. Rerank often requires multiple forward passes; we can model as N*inference where N is candidates. We'll need average candidate count in your logs.
[11:38] Jordan: On security: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs. How quickly can we get those artifacts?
[11:57] Alex: We will share SOC2 summary and network diagram today. SAML and KMS integrations are supported; we'll map the flows. Audit logs are available in the Console with export. We'll attach the docs to the shared drive.
[12:18] Lina: A question on fallback: if Dedicated capacity is saturated do you provide automated fallback to hosted models and is that transparent to our app?
[12:35] Samir: Yes, we support policy-based routing. You can set fallback to a compatible hosted model; it can be automatic with percent-based routing. We'll show configuration in the rollout docs. There can be slight differences in latency and model variant.
[12:56] Ben: Regarding network egress: our security team needs to know expected bandwidth during peak test. Any numbers?
[13:10] Samir: Rough estimate: a single request with 200 tokens input+output at UTF-8 ~200 bytes per token is very rough; better to calculate on your actual payload sizes. For 200 QPS * 200 tokens * ~200 bytes = 8GB/s? Sorry that seems off — transcription slip. We'll give you a precise calc in the template (we'll use token -> bytes estimate and average response size).
[13:42] Alex: Quick note — transcript may have small ASR errors, but main point is we'll provide exact compute/bandwidth estimates in the spreadsheet.
[13:56] Priya: For benchmarks we want p50/p95/p99 for latency, throughput curve, and cost per 1k requests. Also want a regression report vs our current model.
[14:15] Alex: Understood. We'll include those metrics. We'll also provide recommended batching and quantization profiles and expected cost/latency tradeoffs.
[14:35] Jordan: Are there limits on concurrent KV sessions per GPU we should know about?
[14:50] Samir: It depends on model size and context length. We'll produce a memory model table: sessions per GPU estimate for different context sizes. For instance, with 1k context and our medium quantized runtime you might see ~80-120 pinned sessions per A100-equivalent; we'll give ranges.
[15:13] Ben: If we want on-prem/private deployment what differences in timeline?
[15:28] Maya: Private tends to add 2-4 weeks for network and security reviews, and on-prem hardware procurement if needed. VPC/private in cloud can be faster (1-2 weeks).
[15:45] Lina: Ok, next steps recap?
[15:50] Alex: Recap: Redwood to send workload template and SOC2/docs today, Samir to prepare sizing scenarios, schedule a 2-hour benchmark window week of 2026-04-06, Gamma to provide anonymized logs by 2026-03-31. Action items noted in the doc.
[16:12] Jordan: Sounds good. One more: can you include cost delta if we use quantized 4-bit models? We care about minimal quality loss.
[16:28] Samir: Yes we'll include quantization profiles and show exact eval diffs. We'll run the eval with float16 and q4 variants and show the tradeoffs.
[16:45] Priya: For the replay harness please include session affinity so multi-turn flows are preserved.
[16:55] Samir: Absolutely — replay will maintain session IDs and KV context.
[17:05] Alex: Anything else?
[17:10] Ben: Nothing from infra right now.
[17:13] Lina: No.
[17:15] Jordan: Good meeting. Thanks.
[17:18] Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll send the template and docs after this call.
